analysis_notes.summary: LM2 Torah 114 is a three-sentence personal testimony with no bechina language whatsoever. The full text records R' Nathan's account of walking with Rebbe Nachman in silence, during which the Rebbe uttered one Yiddish sentence: 'Es hot a panim az me muz zikh fun a hirur zeyer hitn' — it seems that one must guard oneself very much from a hirur (an improper thought or fantasy). Nathan then explains that he understood from the Rebbe's holy speech and movements at that moment that the Rebbe had been shown in his awesome attainments (הַשָּׂגוֹת) the enormity of the damage of hirur (פְּגַם הַהִרְהוּר), which damages exceedingly. The text concludes: 'And it is impossible to describe this in writing.' The teaching contains no bechina equalities of the form 'X is an aspect of Y'. The concepts הִרְהוּר (improper thought) and פְּגַם הַהִרְהוּר (the damage of improper thought) appear, but their relationship is cause-and-effect (the hirur causes the damage) — an eitza relationship, not a bechina. The Rebbe's statement is a practical-ethical warning ('one must guard from'), not an ontological equation between concepts. There are also no candidate concepts that are described as being the same essential nature as one another. No concepts are flagged as missing from the dataset because the text does not employ bechina language that would generate dataset nodes. A gap analysis in the strict sense cannot be performed when there are no packages to add to.
